newsitem.title: EGYPT: EGYPT TO RETRY MILITANTS FOR POLICE KILLING.
newsitem.headline: EGYPT TO RETRY MILITANTS FOR POLICE KILLING.

text.p: Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri has ordered the retrial of five Moslem militants who were acquitted of charges of the 1993 killing of two policemen in southern Egypt, security sources said on Sunday.

They said Emergency Laws in application in Egypt give Ganzouri, in his post as deputy military ruler, the power to cancel the 1995 acquittals because they were passed by an Emergency State Security Court.
The court comes under the jurisdiction of Emergency Laws that were put into effect in Egypt after militant army officers assassinated president Anwar Sadat in 1981.

The sources said the Emergency State Security Court in Cairo's Abbasiya district had acquitted the men of the charges because it said bullets shells found at the scene of the crime did not match those in the defendants' weapons.
The court also released the five men because it said there were no eyewitnesses who placed them at the scene of the crime, which took place in the southern town of Salamoun in 1993.
State Security prosecutors will now refer the five men, who the sources say are members of the militant al-Gama'a al-Islamiyah (Islamic Group), to another State Security Court.

The Gama'a launched a bloody campaign in 1992 to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people, mostly miliants and policemen, have been killed in political violence since then.
